title: Diffusion: Forward Noise and Reverse Algebra

questions.question: What does a forward diffusion step change?
options: It adds schedule-controlled noise to a clean sample
It predicts a class label from the clean sample
It removes noise using a trained U-Net
It changes the image height without changing values
questions.explanation: The forward process constructs x_t from x_0 and supplied noise using alpha_bar_t; denoising belongs to the reverse process.

questions.question: Which quantity controls how much of x₀ remains in `q_sample` at timestep t?
options: The raw beta alone
The cumulative product alpha_bar_t
The number of classes
The DDIM eta value
questions.explanation: The clean coefficient is sqrt(alpha_bar_t), where alpha_bar multiplies all prior alpha values.

questions.question: If the exact noise passed to `q_sample` is known, how does `predict_x0_from_eps` behave?
options: It recovers x₀ up to floating-point roundoff
It always returns pure Gaussian noise
It needs a class label before it can run
It clips every element to [-1,1]
questions.explanation: The function algebraically inverts x_t = sqrt(alpha_bar)x0 + sqrt(1-alpha_bar)epsilon; it is not a learned denoiser.

questions.question: What does `eta=0` mean for the local `ddim_step`?
options: No additional stochastic term is added, so the same inputs repeat exactly
The beta schedule is discarded
The predicted noise is replaced by zeros
The step must move from an earlier to a later timestep
questions.explanation: The local DDIM-style formula uses no random sigma term when eta is zero; the reverse relation still requires t_prev < t.

questions.question: Why must a training record name whether the model predicts epsilon, x₀, or velocity?
options: Each target changes the meaning of the network output and its loss
The target name determines the image file format
Only epsilon targets can use a beta schedule
The target choice changes the number of RGB channels
questions.explanation: The same noisy input can be paired with different parameterizations; a loss and sampler must interpret the prediction consistently.

questions.question: For a schedule with T=20, which timestep vector is valid for a batch?
options: [0, 7, 19] for a three-sample batch
questions.explanation: Timesteps are integer indices in [0,T), so 0, 7, and 19 are valid for T=20 while -1, 20, and fractional values are not.
